title: CAMEL: Co-Designing AI Models and eDRAMs for Efficient On-Device Learning
problem: Training deep neural networks on resource-limited edge devices demands substantial memory and frequent data access, while eDRAM's periodic refresh cycles consume significant power and can degrade overall system performance.
motivation: On-device learning enables AI models to quickly adapt to local user data, improving service quality and latency on edge platforms.
method: The method uses eDRAM (a high-density memory with lower power leakage than SRAM, though it needs periodic refreshing) as the primary on-chip memory for training data. The neural networks themselves are designed using reversible architectures—computations where intermediate values can be recomputed rather than stored—so data doesn't need to be kept long-term. A system called CAMEL coordinates this eDRAM memory with optimized data flow to minimize memory footprint and traffic to the slower off-chip DRAM, and the shortened data lifetime also reduces refresh operations.
key_novelty: The key innovation is designing reversible neural networks that keep training data in eDRAM for minimal time, which eliminates the expensive refresh cycles that normally drain power.
contributions: Reversible DNN architectures that reduce data lifetime and storage costs during training
